title: N-Dimensional Iterated Interval Integrals
description: Generalizes the 2D Fubini bridge to 3D (fully proved) and n-D (axiomatized), showing all orderings of iterated interval integrals are equal for continuous functions on compact boxes.

meta.author: Lean Genius Research
meta.assumptions: 1 axiom: iteratedIntervalIntegral_order_independent (general n-D order independence). The 2D case (recovered from parent) and 3D case (triple_fubini_of_continuous, triple_fubini_yxz_eq_xyz) are fully proved. Only the general Fin-n inductive step is axiomatized, capturing that adjacent transpositions generate all permutations.

Integrability of parameterized integrals — key for avoiding separate measurability lemmas
Continuous functions are integrable on compact sets

originalContributions: Triple Fubini theorem (3D): ∫ z ∫ y ∫ x f = ∫ x ∫ y ∫ z f for continuous f (fully proved, 0 sorries)
Key technique: Integrable.integral_prod_right avoids separate measurability lemmas for parameter integrals
Inductive definition of n-fold iterated interval integral over Fin-n indexed hyperrectangles
2D swap corollary recovered in the Fin-n framework
General n-D order independence axiomatized with proof strategy documented

overview.historicalContext: The question of when iterated integrals can be exchanged goes back to Fubini (1907) and Tonelli (1909). For n-dimensional iterated integrals, the order independence follows by applying 2D transpositions iteratively — since any permutation decomposes into adjacent transpositions. In Lean 4/Mathlib, the 2D case is accessible via MeasureTheory.integral_integral_swap, but extending this to 3D and n-D requires careful handling of parameterized integrals. The key insight discovered here is that Integrable.integral_prod_right provides integrability of the 'inner' integral as a function of the 'outer' variables, avoiding the need for separate measurability lemmas that were originally the bottleneck.
overview.problemStatement: Can the 2D Fubini bridge (GreensTheoremOQ01OQ01) be generalized to n-dimensional iterated interval integrals over hypercubes, showing that all integration orderings are equal for continuous functions?
overview.text: Proves that for continuous f on [a,b]×[c,d]×[e,f'], all orderings of the triple iterated integral are equal. Defines the n-fold iterated integral inductively via Fin n → ℝ and axiomatizes general order independence.
overview.proofStrategy: 3D proof: (1) For each fixed outer variable, swap the inner two via 2D Fubini. (2) Swap the outer two directly using integral_integral_swap on set integrals, with integrability from Integrable.integral_prod_right applied to the 3D box integrable function. (3) Repeat in the other direction. n-D: Define iteratedIntervalIntegral inductively, prove 2D and 3D cases, axiomatize the general swap.
keyInsights: Integrable.integral_prod_right is the key tool: if G : (ℝ×ℝ)×ℝ → ℝ is integrable on the 3D product measure, then (p : ℝ×ℝ) ↦ ∫ y, G(p,y) is integrable on the 2D product — avoiding separate measurability lemmas

The 3D swap uses integral_integral_swap directly on set integrals (after simp_rw with integral_of_le), with the parameterized integrand (x,z) ↦ ∫ y, f x y z whose integrability follows from Integrable.integral_prod_right
The n-D iterated integral over Fin n → ℝ has natural recursive structure: peel off the first dimension, recurse on Fin.tail. This makes 2D and 3D cases special instances.
The general n-D order independence reduces to showing any permutation of Fin n can be implemented by composing 2D swaps — a group-theoretic fact that holds for all symmetric groups
Icc vs Ioc: the integrability from compactness naturally uses Icc measures, while integral_integral_swap needs Ioc; the transfer uses Measure.restrict_mono Ioc_subset_Icc_self
prerequisites: Lebesgue integration: Bochner integral, product measures, Integrable.integral_prod_right
Interval integrals: integral_of_le converting ∫ in a..b to set integral on Ioc
Fin n types: Fin.cons, Fin.tail, Fin.elim0 for Fin-indexed functions

sections.title: Section 1: Integrability Infrastructure
sections.summary: Three private lemmas establish integrability for the Fubini proof. integrable_2d_of_continuous recovers the parent pattern. integrable_3d_reordered shows G((z,x),y) = f(x,y,z) is integrable on the 3D box (key for the (x,z) swap). integrable_3d_natural shows G((x,y),z) = f(x,y,z) is integrable (key for the (y,x) swap). All use ContinuousOn.integrableOn_compact + Measure.restrict_prod_eq_prod_restrict.
sections.mathContext: For continuous $f : \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}$, any rearrangement of coordinates is still continuous, hence integrable on compact boxes. The measure transfer `Measure.restrict_prod_eq_prod_restrict` converts between `volume.restrict (A \times B)` and `(volume.restrict A).prod (volume.restrict B)`.

sections.title: Section 2: Triple Fubini for Continuous Functions
sections.summary: Proves triple_fubini_of_continuous (3-step proof: swap inner xy, swap outer xz via integral_integral_swap, swap inner yz) and triple_fubini_yxz_eq_xyz (swap outer yx directly). Both use Integrable.integral_prod_right to avoid separate measurability lemmas. 0 sorries.
sections.mathContext: For $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ continuous and $a \leq b$, $c \leq d$, $e \leq f'$: $$\int_e^{f'} \int_c^d \int_a^b f(x,y,z)\,dx\,dy\,dz = \int_a^b \int_c^d \int_e^{f'} f(x,y,z)\,dz\,dy\,dx$$ The key step applies `MeasureTheory.integral_integral_swap` with the parameterized integrand $(x,z) \mapsto \int_c^d f(x,y,z)\,dy$, whose integrability follows from `Integrable.integral_prod_right` applied to the 3D-integrable rearrangement $((z,x),y) \mapsto f(x,y,z)$.

sections.title: Section 3: All Key Orderings Are Equal
sections.summary: triple_fubini_all_equal combines the two swap theorems: all three 'outer-variable' orderings (z-first, z-first-then-x-first, y-first) equal the canonical (x,y,z) ordering. Proved directly from the two swap theorems and the parent 2D Fubini.
sections.mathContext: Any ordering reachable by a sequence of 2D transpositions equals the canonical ordering. For 3 variables, all 6 permutations are generated by the adjacent transpositions (xy) and (yz).

sections.title: Sections 4-5: N-Dimensional Iterated Integral
sections.summary: Defines iteratedIntervalIntegral : (Fin n → ℝ) → (Fin n → ℝ) → ((Fin n → ℝ) → ℝ) → ℝ by induction. Proves n=1 and n=2 special cases. iteratedIntervalIntegral_two_swap recovers 2D Fubini in the Fin framework. iteratedIntervalIntegral_order_independent axiomatizes general n-D order independence with documented proof strategy.
sections.mathContext: The n-fold iterated integral over $[a_0,b_0] \times \cdots \times [a_{n-1},b_{n-1}]$ is defined by: $$I_n(a,b,f) = \int_{a_0}^{b_0} I_{n-1}(\text{Fin.tail}(a), \text{Fin.tail}(b), x' \mapsto f(\text{Fin.cons}(x_0, x')))\,dx_0$$ General order independence follows from the fact that $S_n$ is generated by adjacent transpositions, and each adjacent transposition is an instance of 2D Fubini.

Companion: Ioo integrability suffices for the 2D Fubini swap

conclusion.summary: YES: the 2D Fubini bridge generalizes to 3D with a fully proved result (0 sorries), and to n-D with the recursive definition of iteratedIntervalIntegral and the general order independence axiomatized. The key technique — Integrable.integral_prod_right — avoids separate measurability lemmas that were the original bottleneck.
conclusion.implications: For continuous functions on compact boxes, iterated interval integrals are order-independent in any dimension. The 3D case is immediately applicable to physics (triple integrals in vector calculus). The Fin-n framework provides a foundation for formalizing multivariable integration theorems.
openQuestions: Can iteratedIntervalIntegral_order_independent be proved by induction using Integrable.integral_prod_right at each step, closing the remaining axiom?
Can Mathlib's Marginal API (lmarginal_union) be used to give a cleaner proof of the n-D case?
Does the proof extend to non-continuous (merely integrable) functions using appropriate DCT hypotheses?
